title: GENII Publisher sync envelope
description: What a publication offers to synchronize, materialized for a client to fetch. A declaration that reaches nothing is decoration, and this is how the declaration reaches the code that acts on it.

buildId.description: The reader artifact's build identity, carried verbatim, so every artifact of one build agrees on it.

consent.description: Pinned, and carried into the artifact rather than left implicit, so a client cannot be built against a publication that quietly relaxed it.

localFallback.description: Also pinned. Synchronizing is additive to local reading, never a precondition for it, so a reader who declines or cannot reach the provider still reads.

package.description: The provider a publication declared, recorded and never executed.

provider.description: Deliberately has no config field, and additionalProperties is false, so provider configuration cannot reach this artifact even by mistake. This file is served publicly. A provider config is author-supplied and may hold a project reference, an endpoint, or a key that was never meant to leave the repository, and a rule that says so is a rule somebody eventually forgets. Making it structurally impossible costs nothing: configuration stays in the publication manifest, which is not published, and reaches the provider through the host's own environment.
